advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CI-gating (non-integration) test that distinguishes scc's `Lines` from `Code` — e.g. feed the stub/adapter a payload where blank lines make `Lines != Code` and assert the adapter reports `Lines`.
evidence: test_live_reported_loc_matches_wc_l is guarded: `@pytest.mark.integration` + `@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("scc") is None, reason="scc is not installed")` (tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc_heldout.py:227-229)

CI runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (default suite) and `pytest -m integration` (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:594,607); no workflow installs scc — `search_files('.github/workflows', 'scc')` returns no matches, so the integration tier runs without scc and every skipif fires

The CI-running stub in tests/interfaces/metrics_polyglot_support.py emits both `"Lines": len(lines)` and `"Code": sum(1 for line in lines if line.strip())` (lines 127-128), but the polyglot fixtures have no blank lines: tests/fixtures/metrics_polyglot/python/src/main.py is 4 non-blank lines and typescript/src/main.ts is 6 non-blank lines, so Lines==Code and reading `Code` would still yield the same max_loc the test asserts (test_metrics_polyglot.py:36-41)
advisory.finding: The load-bearing AC4 semantic reconciliation — that per-file LOC reads scc's `Lines` (== `wc -l`) and NOT `Code` (which never equals `wc -l`) — is verified only by `@pytest.mark.integration` + `@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which('scc') is None)` tests, and scc is installed in NO CI workflow, so these tests always skip. The one CI-running stub-backed test (`tests/interfaces/test_metrics_polyglot.py`) uses fixture files with zero blank lines, where `Lines == Code`, so it cannot distinguish the two fields. The unit tests feed payloads containing only a `Lines` key, catching the field-name switch but not the semantic wc-l equivalence. A regression that re-reads `Code` semantics would pass every gating CI test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Give at least one polyglot fixture file (or the default-runner unit test's stub payload) blank lines so `Lines != Code`, and assert the reported LOC equals the raw line count, not the `Code` value — in a test that runs in the default (non-integration) suite.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or enforce) that scc `Lines` equals `wc -l`/`count(\n)` only when every measured file ends in a newline, or reconcile the two counts explicitly for files lacking a trailing newline.
evidence: tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_module_size_reconciliation_heldout.py:84 `assert measured == gate_files, "per-file LOC must equal the gate's wc -l count"`
Ticket/commit claim: '0 mismatches over all 436 files' — an empirical, tree-dependent claim, not an invariant (a file without a final newline makes scc Lines = count(\n)+1).
dropped.finding: The scc->CI-gate reconciliation equates scc's `Lines` (physical line count) with `text.count("\n")` (newline count). These differ by one for any file that lacks a trailing newline: scc `Lines` counts the final unterminated line while `count("\n")` does not. The equality (`measured == gate_files`) holds only empirically for the current tree (all files end in a newline) and would break if any `src/rebar/**/*.py` file ever omits its final newline.
scenarios: A new or edited src/rebar Python file is committed without a trailing newline; the held-out reconciliation test flips red even though both the metric and the gate are individually correct.
